My Lord, just before we proceed, can I raise one matter with your Lordship? We're grateful to the staff caring for Ms Letby for passing on to us, via Ms Clancy in the first instance, that Ms Letby has not been feeling well.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: She says she's not been feeling well.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: She says she's not been feeling well, hasn't eaten, but wants to continue, as I understand the position. That's what she would like to do. Naturally, in all the circumstances, that message causes concern to us, that, at the very least, we and the court are satisfied that she is in a proper state to continue.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: And I don't know whether it's a matter of which your Lordship needs to make any enquiry. Obviously we cannot make any enquiry in the circumstances. But in any event, it's something we need to bring to your Lordship's attention so it's watched carefully.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: We consider it would be helpful to have it confirmed with the witness, Ms Letby, that she is able to continue having received the message that we have, and that's for her benefit and everyone's benefit.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, exactly. I will do that.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I gather you're not feeling very well?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Do you feel well enough to continue?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. We will continue then. Should there come a time when you genuinely feel you are not fit to continue, would you please indicate and we will then pause the proceedings?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, my Lord. May we raise concerns if we see anything that concerns us with your Lordship?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, certainly. It's a difficult balance to strike --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: It is.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: -- but the process must continue, but obviously not if she is unfit to give evidence.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: My Lord, yes.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON (continued)
Mr Johnson.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: My Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: We're going to move on, please, to count 20, which concerns [Baby O]. As before, I'd like to start with the contents of your defence statement, so if you just want to put that thing away. Page 21, I hope, will take you to paragraph 168.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: It reads as follows:
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: "I did nothing to hurt [Baby O]."
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: "On 23 June 2016 I was allocated [Baby O], [Baby P] and another baby called J. Rebecca Morgan, the student nurse who was with me, fed [Baby O] at 8.30, 10.30 and 12.30. I signed the notes for this but she fed him down the NG tube and did his observations. Shortly after the 12.30 feed, [Baby O] vomited, he
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: didn't look right, and his observations were yellow on the charts."
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: And I assume that by yellow, you're referring to the -- in the yellow entry on the chart.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "It had not been a profound vomit, however because [Baby O] didn't look right I got [Dr A] to review him, this will have been around 13.50, and nil by mouth was entered in the medical notes. At that point, there was a change in his appearance but it was not dramatic. [Baby O] remained in nursery 2."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So, so far, is what I have read to you what appears in the document?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And is it correct?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "At 14.40 [Baby O]'s monitors went off. He was not breathing well and his tummy was red and distended. I'd done nothing to cause this to happen. I called [Dr A] from nursery 3 and he used the Neopuff. He checked the blood gas, which was not good, and so we moved [Baby O] to nursery 1. Too many babies in there and so we had to move some out [as read]."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Again, is that what it says?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And is it correct?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "When [Baby O] collapsed people were panicking. The unit was very busy. We had to move another baby to make space for [Baby O] in nursery 1."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that what it says?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is it correct?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "When [Baby O] was put on the ventilator in nursery 1, he stabilised but then deteriorated rapidly."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Again, is that what it says?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And is it correct?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "I didn't notice a rash to the right side of [Baby O]'s chest. No one mentioned such a rash. His hands and feet were pale and his stomach was red and purpuric and getting bigger all the time. At one point Dr Brearey put a needle into his stomach to see if anything could be drained. My recollection is that his stomach stayed red the whole time. I was present when we were resuscitating [Baby O] and it did not go."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So again, is that what it says?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And is it correct?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "[Baby O]'s abdomen was very swollen and the doctors were struggling to get access to a vein. One of [Baby O]'s lines had tissued and we were struggling to get lines into him. His peripheries turned white. He was so poorly it couldn't be done and the only option was to inject his shin and put a line into his leg."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that what it says?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And is that correct?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Are you there suggesting that intravenous access was lost?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm saying that one of his lines had tissued, yes. One of the lines.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Are you saying that intravenous access was lost?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't say. From that I've read one of [Baby O]'s lines had tissued.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You know the significance of intravenous access in this case, don't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, we'll come to it. 177:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "[Dr B] kept going outside to smoke during the collapse. I appreciate it may seem a small matter in all the circumstances, but she didn't wash her hands when she returned."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that what it says?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And is that true?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then finally:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Sophie Ellis had raised a concern about [Baby O] and the appearance of his abdomen during the night shift before my shift commenced. I do not accept that this was dealt with adequately at the time."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that what it says?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And is that true?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And is that your position, that you do not accept it was dealt with adequately at the time?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: When did you come to that conclusion?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: By the time this statement had been written.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What was it that caused you to reach that conclusion?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Reviewing all of the medical records.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So that is some time at or before, I think it was, 11 February that this document was signed off, 2022?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. That date is on the final page if anyone wants to check it.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: All right. One thing I've overlooked is the question I ask you usually at the beginning of every day or every session, namely: up to this point in your evidence, is there anything that you want to amend or change or put a different emphasis on?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So taking yesterday as the most recent example, is there anything you said yesterday that you now wish to review?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Anything you felt you couldn't answer yesterday that, having thought about it overnight, you now feel that perhaps you can answer?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Have you given that some thought?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I've thought about it overnight, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, you have thought about what you said yesterday and whether or not in fact you made a mistake; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I want to deal with the background to [Baby O]'s death, please. We know from the evidence that we have heard that he was born on Tuesday, 21 June at 14.24. He died on Thursday, 23 June at 17.47. All right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: At the time of [Baby O]'s birth, you were abroad, weren't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You were with [Nurse E] and others in Ibiza?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You had gone there on 20 June and you returned on the 22nd?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And you were very interested in the triplets, even before you had seen them, weren't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I received information about the triplets, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Would it be fair to say that they were big news in the unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, it was very unusual to have triplets on the unit, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Naturally conceived triplets. Had you ever in your experience come across naturally conceived triplets?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If Mr Murphy would help, please, and we start at tile 21, this is your friend Jennifer Jones-Key telling you about their arrival; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: In the next text you make it clear that, as a matter of fact, you already knew.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then we have tile 24 where you say:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Probably be back in with a bang."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Within 72 hours of that text, the two [Surname of Babies O, P & R] boys were dead and [Baby Q] had collapsed; that's right, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And all happened when you were there?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. You then texted your friend [Dr A] at tile 62, please -- I say text, it's a Facebook message -- still on the 22nd, where you were asking him for further detail about the triplets.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Any reason why you were so interested?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It was general conversation. Triplets were unusual.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Jennifer had obviously text me to say they were born, as had [Dr A]. It was just general conversation about something that's quite unusual.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did you want to get involved with them?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I'm just making enquiries about something that's unusual on the unit that other members of staff are talking to me about.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you accept the evidence of the boys' mother, [Mother of Babies O, P & R], that all went well at their birth?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you accept that overnight, the day they were born, the 21st into 22 June, Amy Davies told us that there were no concerns for either [Baby O] or [Baby P]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you accept the evidence of Samantha O'Brien from the day shift on 22 June, so the day that you were sending the texts we've just looked at, when she said that [Baby O] in particular was fine on that day shift?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And Yvonne Farmer, who said he was moved into nursery 2 because he was doing so well on that shift?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you accept that overnight, from the 22nd into 23 June, both [Baby O] and [Baby P] were clinically well?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that on this, on the 22nd?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This is the day before -- this is the night shift before you came in on the 23rd.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And do you accept that they were moved from CPAP to Optiflow on that night shift?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'd have to check. I can't recall that from memory, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We'll come to the charts. Chris Booth told us that his impression was that [Baby O] would "sail through". Until [Baby O] collapsed, did you see anything to undermine that as a reasonable impression?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, not up until that lunchtime, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Sophie Ellis actually looked after [Baby O] in particular that night and said that there was nothing concerning about his presentation; do you accept that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If you go, please, to jury bundle 2, which is, in your case, the one with the big blue 2 on the spine, and go to divider 20, please, you will find the charts and other documentation for [Baby O].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If you look at the second page, which is J23657, there we have the observation chart for [Baby O] from about the time of his birth; do you see that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And thus the clock went from the 21st to the 22nd, about halfway across the page, where we get to midnight.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do you see that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It ran to 13.00 hours on the 22nd at the far right of the page.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then over the page, on page 23658, we have a chart starting at 14.00 hours on 22 June and moving through to the early hours and then ultimately the time of death of [Baby O]'s death on 23 June.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: In answer to questions asked by your counsel, I just want to confirm that you identified your handwriting on that chart, in particular where we see what looks like 13.30; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that a time that's been changed as a matter of interest?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It looks like I've gone over it in some way, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It looks like there was a 4 there at some stage, doesn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't -- I can't say for definite.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, it's your writing. What does it look like to you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You might be better looking at the screen in fact because it's enlarged on the screen.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I would say it's gone from a 2 to a 3.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. So no 4 under there?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: That -- that's my opinion, it's a 2 to a 4.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Anyway, we know that problems for [Baby O] started, give or take, at about lunchtime, at about 13.15; all right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We'll come to it in the sequence, but looking at the readings, the observations, is there anything concerning, from your perspective, on that chart prior to that time that I have just drawn your attention to?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: His temperature's a little bit unstable at times.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, someone appears to have put a reading into the temperature chart at 12.30 and then crossed it out, don't they, and put a different one in?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Was that you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: How can you say?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's not how I would document a temperature. That's not my writing.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That dot is not your writing?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't believe so, no, because I join up -- I usually join up the arrows.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Like you didn't do at 14.30 or 13.30?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Because they're not a direct continuation. When there's two side by side, usually you should join them up, which is what's been done in the yellow bit. They actually join up.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I think you'll have to keep your voice up, if you can, please.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: [Baby O], according to that chart, had been very stable overnight, hadn't he?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: He's had some temperature issues, but yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Looking just -- if we can look at the bottom part of the page, please, Mr Murphy. That's it, thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That left-hand column under where it says "Cooling infant", do you see it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It says "sats" and then "fractional oxygen".
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then what does it say?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Optiflow."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. And this is the point I made to you earlier, that [Baby O] had been on Optiflow for quite some time, hadn't he, by the time --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. I couldn't recall that from my memory, so thank you for showing me.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It's quite all right. It may be important, all right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: His ECG leads had been removed and that would be in keeping with this picture, wouldn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, if that's what happened, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That was the evidence.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: His antibiotics had been stopped and we know from tile 175, if Mr Murphy would help, please, that in a sample taken after his first collapse at 13.39, after 5 days there was no bacterial infection.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we then go, please, to tile 52, or in the paper version to 23958. An incorrect reference there. 23676.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That's my mistake.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't think we have a paper version of either of those.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: It's 23661. It's my mistake in my note, my Lord. 23661.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Four from the back.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we could scroll down just a little bit, please, Mr Murphy. The aspirates in the output section under the NG/asp/vomit column show that [Baby O] was tolerating his feeds very well, don't they?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Going back to your defence statement then, and what you wrote at paragraph 178, what are you saying is the point that you don't accept that the appearance of his abdomen overnight was dealt with adequately?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think concerns were raised about his abdomen and feeds were continued.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But what was actually going on shows that there wasn't a problem, doesn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I -- I don't know.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, you do know, you're a band 5 QIS qualified nurse.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Where, looking at the data, is the problem?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I -- I can't say without looking.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, you take your time and look and you tell us where you are saying this problem was.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: (Pause)
He's still having milky aspirates.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You give us the page that you're looking at, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So if we carry on in the documents to the final document behind divider 20, what's the problem?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: There's not a problem, it's just that he is still having aspirates and he hasn't had his bowels open.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Doesn't it say bowels opened, for example, at 5 o'clock, and he passed urine as well?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think that's a BNO.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: BNO?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, you see, this is one of the reasons I went to your defence statement first because you raise an issue and I'll just remind you of what you said at paragraph 178:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Sophie Ellis raised a concern about [Baby O] and the appearance of his abdomen during the night shift. I do not accept that this was dealt with adequately."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What is the inadequacy?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't know.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You don't know?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So you are suggesting that there was a problem but you can't -- you're not in a position to tell us what the problem was?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Mm.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is that what it comes to?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And there's no apparent problem recorded in the paperwork; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, not on the charts, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you accept Dr Mayberry's account of examining [Baby O] at the end of the night shift and that all was well?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is this the night when he reviewed him but didn't write the notes?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, it is.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: So yes, on his word, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. Well, are you suggesting we shouldn't accept his word if he didn't write it down himself?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I'm saying there's no way of definitively knowing if he reviewed him or not.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, Sophie Ellis wrote down that he had because, as you remember, I'm sure, he had been called away and didn't have time to make the note himself.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So when you say there's no way of definitively knowing, if he didn't examine him, would it follow you're suggesting
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: there must have been some sort of cover-up between Dr Mayberry and Sophie Ellis?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON
